6.q: A project involves activities that must meet current regulatory requirements, and the project manager needs to be confident the compliance information they rely on is accurate and up to date. Which source is best for up-to-date information on regulatory compliance?
6.w: Official government sources publish current legislation and regulatory guidance and are updated when the rules change, so they are the most reliable source of up-to-date compliance information.

n.1: Textbooks are useful background but can be out of date once regulations change.
n.2: Supplier brochures promote products and may present regulations selectively.
n.3: A previous project's checklist may be out of date and may not match this project's activities.
n.4: Trade press summaries can lag behind changes and simplify the detail.

6.q: A project manager is assessing the risks of using a predictive (linear) life cycle on an initiative operating in a changing business environment. Which of the following is a limitation of the predictive (linear) life cycle in this context?
o: It struggles with adapting to change
It is incompatible with fixed budgets
It delays delivery of any value
It allows too much scope creep
6.w: Linear life cycles are inflexible to change once planning is complete.

n.0: Governance is usually strong in linear cycles.
n.2: Fixed budgets are well supported.
n.3: While delivery is at the end, it doesn’t inherently delay value.
n.4: Scope is tightly managed in predictive models.

6.q: A steering group receives a project report in which every activity is shown as 'green', despite the fact that several delays are already well known to the delivery team. What does this discrepancy most clearly indicate?
o: The project manager is reducing unnecessary detail
The project is performing well overall
The reporting system is highly efficient
Status reporting is not accurately reflecting project reality
6.w: Misleading status indicators undermine transparency and decision-making.

6.q: A project manager is looking for ways to keep the delivery team motivated and performing well throughout a demanding project. Which TWO leadership behaviours are MOST likely to improve motivation and project team performance?
o: Providing clear objectives and explaining the purpose behind the work
Avoiding difficult conversations to maintain short-term harmony
Using pressure as the main method of sustaining delivery pace
Increasing control over every task regardless of team competence
Giving timely feedback that helps individuals improve
6.w: Clear purpose and useful feedback help team members understand expectations, improve capability and sustain motivation.

n.1: Avoiding difficult conversations can allow performance issues to continue.
n.2: Pressure alone may produce short-term effort but often damages sustainable performance.
n.3: Excessive control can reduce autonomy and motivation.

6.q: When assigning roles on a new project, a project manager must ensure that no team member is treated unfairly because of an attribute protected under equality law. Considering the options below, a project manager must avoid discrimination based on which of the following characteristics?
6.w: Age is one of the nine protected characteristics under the Equality Act 2010, so roles must not be assigned less favourably because of it.

n.0: A home postcode is not a protected characteristic, though relying on it could indirectly disadvantage some groups.
n.1: Socio-economic status is not one of the nine protected characteristics under the Equality Act 2010.
n.3: Body weight is not a protected characteristic in itself, unless it relates to a disability.
n.4: Length of service is not a protected characteristic, although it can relate to other employment rights.

6.q: As a project moves towards closure, the sponsor wants assurance that the intended value will continue to be monitored once the outputs are in operational use. Which approach BEST ensures benefits are effectively tracked after project delivery?
o: Including benefits within the project schedule as milestones
Relying on informal feedback from stakeholders after delivery
Assigning clear benefit owners and defining measurable indicators
Transferring all responsibility to the project manager post-closure
Reviewing benefits only at the final project stage gate
6.w: Clear ownership and measurable metrics are essential for tracking benefits over time.

n.0: Milestones track outputs, not ongoing benefits realisation.
n.1: Informal feedback lacks structure and measurable tracking.
n.3: Benefits ownership typically transfers to business stakeholders.
n.4: Single-stage reviews are insufficient for tracking ongoing benefits.

6.q: Which TWO outcomes are expected when applying resource levelling?
6.w: Levelling balances demand but often extends duration.

n.1: Costs may increase.
n.3: Not directly affected.
n.4: Risks remain.

6.q: A project is reaching its end, but a small number of supplier invoices remain unpaid because their amounts are being disputed. As project manager preparing for financial closure, what is the recommended approach?
o: Transfer unpaid invoices to a future project
Resolve all payment disputes before final closure
6.w: All financial issues, including disputes, must be resolved before closure.

n.0: Funds must be managed according to agreement.
n.1: Accounts should not be closed until obligations are met.
n.2: Each project’s finances must be kept separate.
n.3: Ignoring payments is not acceptable.

6.q: At the very start of a novel research and development project, little detailed information is available and uncertainty is high. The organisation has never run a comparable project and holds no relevant historical data, but several experienced specialists are available. Which estimating approach is most appropriate for the initial concept-phase cost estimate?
o: Delphi estimating using anonymous expert rounds
Earned value forecasting from progress to date
Parametric estimating from historical unit rates
Analogous estimating from a similar past project
6.w: With no comparable project or historical data, analogous and parametric methods have no basis, and there is no detailed WBS yet for bottom-up estimating. Delphi gathers anonymous expert judgement over several facilitated rounds to reach a consensus, avoiding dominant voices.

n.1: Earned value forecasts from progress against a baseline; no work has been done yet.
n.2: Parametric estimating needs reliable historical data, which this novel project lacks.
n.3: Bottom-up estimating needs a detailed WBS, which does not exist at concept.
n.4: Analogous estimating needs a genuinely comparable past project, and there is none.

6.q: A project team updates all data sources but forgets to communicate process changes to operations. Which is NOT an effective mitigation in this scenario?
6.w: Skipping the operations handover would ignore the core issue and lead to further delays.

n.0: End-user training ensures operations understand new processes.
n.1: Cutover updates can include handover steps for operations.
n.3: A communication plan directly addresses the lack of messaging.
n.4: Documenting support processes clarifies how operations should proceed.

6.q: During a lessons-learned review, a project manager wants to highlight the benefits that well-managed conflict brought to the team over the life cycle. When considering the potential positive impacts of conflict on a project, which of the following is NOT one of them?
6.w: Reduced communication is a negative consequence, not a positive impact.

n.0: Enhanced innovation is a positive impact.
n.2: Greater engagement is a positive impact.
n.3: Stronger solutions can result from conflict.
n.4: Improved decision making is a positive impact.

6.q: Which two factors capture quality performance in project reporting?
o: Change request count and audit frequency
Procurement lead time and team turnover rate
6.w: Defect density and rework hours directly measure product quality and correction effort.

n.0: Satisfaction and risks relate to stakeholders/risk, not quality.
n.2: Change requests/audits are process controls, not quality metrics.
n.3: Schedule and cost variances measure time and budget.
n.4: Procurement and turnover are unrelated to quality performance.

6.q: Which TWO are key limitations of written communication?
6.w: Written communication can be misinterpreted and lacks interaction.

n.0: It does not ensure engagement.
n.1: This is an advantage, not a limitation.
n.3: Written communication does not provide instant feedback.

6.q: A project manager is selecting an appropriate response for a threat identified in the risk register. Considering the standard responses available for threats, which of the following is NOT one of them?
6.w: Exploit is a response for positive risks (opportunities), not threats.

n.1: Acceptance is for threats as well as opportunities.
n.2: Reduction manages threats.
n.3: Avoid is a threat response.
n.4: Transfer is for threats.

6.q: Sponsors request concise summaries while developers need in-depth technical data. The project manager must adjust the level of ______ to meet these needs.
6.w: Varying the level of detail ensures summaries remain concise or comprehensive as appropriate.

n.0: Timelines define schedules, not level of information.
n.1: Scope defines work boundaries, not message granularity.
n.3: Resource allocation covers assets, not messaging detail.
n.4: Budget relates to costs, not communication depth.

6.q: Whether a project uses a linear or an iterative life cycle, a consistent activity is applied to determine whether a proposed change should go ahead. Which process is used in both linear and iterative life cycles to decide whether a change should be made?
o: Evaluation of the change's impact and benefits
Unanimous approval by the project team
6.w: All approaches evaluate impact and benefits before making decisions on changes.

n.0: Documentation is vital in change control.
n.2: Team input is important but not the only factor.
n.3: Stakeholder input is essential.
n.4: Immediate implementation skips proper control.

6.q: A project manager is drawing up the agenda for a business case review meeting with the sponsor and steering group. Checking the proposed items, which one is NOT typically part of a business case review meeting?
6.w: Walking through test scripts is a detailed quality control activity; a business case review looks at whether benefits still outweigh costs and risks.

n.1: Changes in risk affect the justification.
n.2: Benefit forecasts are central to the business case.
n.3: Cost variances affect viability.
n.4: Checking assumptions confirms the case is still valid.

6.q: Which characteristic best defines a well-structured WBS?
o: Hierarchical decomposition of deliverables into manageable work packages
6.w: A WBS breaks down deliverables hierarchically into manageable components.

6.q: When setting up the risk register and issue log, a project manager names a specific individual as owner for each entry rather than leaving them unassigned. Why is it important to assign ownership for each risk and issue in this way?
o: It guarantees the risk or issue will not occur
It ensures accountability for monitoring and managing them
It eliminates the need for escalation
It removes risks from the register automatically
6.w: Assigning ownership makes someone responsible for monitoring and acting on each risk or issue.

n.0: Ownership supports management, not prevention.
n.2: Escalation may still be needed for major risks/issues.
n.3: Accountability is the main benefit, not just more paperwork.
n.4: Risks are removed only when resolved or closed.

6.q: A commercial project is releasing a Minimum Marketable Product to customers early in an iterative delivery. A benefit of using an MMP in this way is that:
o: It reduces the need for change management
It allows early revenue and real-world validation
It delays user involvement until project closure
It guarantees all requirements will be met immediately
6.w: MMP enables market launch and testing of real-world value early.

n.0: Change management is still required.
n.1: Stakeholder sign-off is always important.
n.3: User involvement should be early and ongoing.
n.4: All requirements are not delivered at once.

6.q: A newly appointed team leader is studying McGregor's Theory X to understand the assumptions it makes about how workers behave and how they should be managed. Which of these is NOT a principle of Theory X?
6.w: Theory X assumes people dislike work and need direction; the idea that employees are self-motivated contradicts Theory X.

n.0: Close supervision is characteristic of Theory X managers.
n.1: Under Theory X, people are seen as preferring direction over autonomy.
n.3: Theory X holds that workers avoid responsibility.
n.4: Theory X views work as undesirable and employees as reluctant.

6.q: Which two contract types are classified as cost-reimbursement agreements?
6.w: Both cost-plus fee and target cost reimburse actual costs, with differing fee structures.

n.0: Fixed-price and per-unit do not reimburse actual costs.
n.1: Target cost is cost-reimbursement but per-unit is unit-rate.
n.2: Lump-sum is a fixed-price variant.
n.4: Per-unit focuses on quantity, not cost reimbursement.

6.q: Midway through a project, market conditions and internal priorities have shifted significantly, and the sponsor has convened a decision gate to confirm whether the project should continue. Which TWO factors should be reassessed at this gate to confirm ongoing viability?
6.w: Decision gates reassess costs and benefits to confirm ongoing viability.

n.0: Location is irrelevant.
n.2: Morale is not a primary decision factor.
n.4: Communication frequency is not central.

6.q: An organisation is documenting how problems that cannot be resolved at working level are formally raised and dealt with under its governance arrangements. Complete the statement: a governance framework defines the _______ for raising and resolving project issues.
6.w: The escalation process defines how issues beyond a role's tolerance are formally raised to the right level and resolved.

n.0: The work breakdown structure breaks the scope into work packages.
n.1: A configuration audit checks items against their records and requirements.
n.2: A resource histogram shows resource demand over time.
n.3: A benefits profile describes a benefit and how it will be measured.

6.q: A project engages a supplier for support services whose volume will vary over time, and the buyer wants to be billed according to the hours and resources actually used. Which reimbursement method is most suitable for scalable services billed by usage?
6.w: Time-and-materials allows billing based on hours or units of service used.

n.0: Per-unit is for discrete physical units, not service hours.
n.1: Target cost sets a baseline, not usage billing.
n.2: Fixed-price is a total sum, not usage-based.
n.4: Cost-plus is cost reimbursement, not usage billing.

6.q: A project is falling behind because key resources are becoming bottlenecks, with too much work converging on them at once. Before seeking more budget or people, what is the most appropriate immediate action for the project manager to take?
o: Re-sequence activities to reduce demand on constrained resources
Request additional budget to hire more resources
Escalate to stakeholders before analysing the problem
Pause the project until the bottleneck clears
Increase the frequency of project status reporting
6.w: Re-sequencing can alleviate bottlenecks without requiring additional resources.

n.1: Budget may not solve availability.
n.2: Escalation without analysis is premature.
n.3: Pausing is excessive.
n.4: Monitoring does not resolve constraints.

6.q: A project support officer is compiling a checklist of the activities that make up their organisation's project governance, and one proposed item does not seem to belong. Which of the following is NOT a typical governance activity?
6.w: Informal social activities are not a formal part of governance procedures.

n.0: Risk assessments are a key governance control.
n.2: Charter approval is a core governance milestone.
n.3: Defining roles is fundamental to governance.
n.4: Reporting processes enforce accountability.

6.q: A member of a virtual project team has delivered strong results but confides that their achievements go unnoticed because they are rarely seen at the office. The team leader wants to keep this person motivated and engaged. How should leadership respond?
o: Regularly acknowledge and celebrate remote contributions
6.w: Recognition is crucial for remote staff to feel valued and engaged.

n.0: Remote members must not be overlooked.
n.1: Recognition supports morale.
n.3: Meetings help build team identity.
n.4: All achievements should be acknowledged.

6.q: A significant change request has been raised that would affect the project's scope, timescale and budget, and it is unclear who should decide on it. Which responsibility is typically shared between the project manager and the sponsor?
o: Completing all individual team member performance reviews
Installing and configuring the technical tools and software
Maintaining the issue log and daily progress records
Approving changes that impact scope, time, or cost
Drafting the detailed content of each work package
6.w: Major changes must be escalated and agreed upon by both the PM and sponsor.

n.0: Performance reviews are a line management responsibility.
n.1: Technical setup is not a governance responsibility.
n.2: The issue log is maintained by the PM or project support.
n.4: Work packages are typically created by workstream leads.

7.q: Which TWO elements should a communication plan define clearly?
7.w: A communication management plan sets out who needs information (stakeholder groups), what they need and why, and when and how often it is provided, in what format, through which channel and from whom.

n.0: Activity duration estimates belong in the schedule, not the communication plan.
n.1: Supplier evaluation criteria belong in the procurement strategy, not the communication plan.
n.4: Risk response owners are recorded in the risk register.

7.q: A team is described as having complementary skills, shared accountability, and a commitment to common goals. Which model highlights these features?
7.w: Katzenbach and Smith focus on skills, accountability, and purpose in team effectiveness.

n.0: Myers-Briggs focuses on personality types.
n.1: Belbin focuses on behavioural team roles.
n.3: Tuckman outlines team stages.
n.4: Margerison McCann looks at work preferences.

7.q: When auditors discover that the project's risk logs are incomplete, the assurance mandate includes validating the ______ of such records throughout the project.
7.w: Assurance verifies that all required risk information is complete and up to date.

n.0: Efficiency is a performance metric, not directly completeness.
n.1: Popularity is irrelevant to risk documentation.
n.2: Creativity is not an assurance criterion.
n.4: Redundancy refers to duplication, not thoroughness.

7.q: Which TWO features define an extended life cycle?
o: A focus on delivering outputs only
7.w: The extended life cycle (BoK7) adds adoption and benefits realisation phases after transition, so the life cycle continues until the benefits in the business case are realised.

n.1: Users and the sponsor stay closely involved to adopt the outputs and realise benefits.
n.2: The project life cycle ends at handover; the extended life cycle carries on past it.
n.4: It extends beyond outputs to their adoption and the benefits they enable.

7.q: Which situation most strongly supports a hybrid life cycle?
7.w: Hybrid suits projects with both predictable and uncertain elements.

n.1: Governance is still needed.
n.2: This suits linear.
n.3: Stakeholders are required.
n.4: This is linear.

7.q: A retailer is investing in a project to streamline its warehouse operations, and the project team is defining scope by distinguishing deliverables from the improvements the business expects to gain. In this situation, which of the following best describes a benefit when defining project scope?
o: Enhanced business efficiency resulting from project changes
The creation of a cost baseline
7.w: A benefit is a measurable improvement resulting from project outcomes, such as business efficiency.

n.0: A project status report is a deliverable, not a benefit.
n.2: A breakdown of project tasks is part of planning, not a benefit.
n.3: Meetings are a project activity, not a benefit.
n.4: A cost baseline is a planning tool.

7.q: Which of the following best describes unconscious bias?
o: A deliberate decision to exclude someone
A preference or prejudice that operates without conscious awareness
7.w: Unconscious bias is an unintentional, automatic tendency to favour or exclude.

n.0: Deliberate exclusion is conscious, not unconscious.
n.1: Project objectives do not relate to bias.
n.3: Stakeholder analysis is a project management tool.
n.4: Policies are formal documents, not biases.

7.q: What is the primary trade-off when applying resource levelling?
7.w: Levelling trades schedule duration against resource constraints.

n.1: Not applicable.
n.2: Irrelevant.
n.3: Indirect relationship.
n.4: Not the core trade-off.

7.q: A healthcare provider implements an electronic records system. Which pair should be documented in the benefits management plan to ensure data accuracy and user adoption?
7.w: Metrics define accuracy measures and training supports user adoption.

n.0: Risk and issue logs relate to risk management.
n.1: Charter and scope are project initiation outputs.
n.3: Budget estimates are cost data, not specific improvements.
n.4: Communication and quality may support but don't directly target those goals.

7.q: A project manager is deciding which information the board most needs in order to judge whether a proposed project is genuinely viable. Which TWO components are essential for assessing project viability in a business case?
7.w: Cost and benefit are fundamental to viability assessment.

7.q: A project professional working in the UK must ensure their project complies with the requirements of GDPR when processing personal data. Which source is best for authoritative advice on meeting these obligations?
7.w: ICO is the UK's regulatory authority for data protection and GDPR.

n.0: Business news is not authoritative for GDPR compliance.
n.1: Gossip is not reliable.
n.2: Blogs may not be accurate.
n.4: Forums are not official sources.

7.q: A capable project team finds itself waiting for sign-off on routine, low-value tasks because approvals must always pass upward, and delivery is slipping as a result. What is the most likely governance issue?
o: Authority has not been delegated appropriately
7.w: Poor delegation leads to unnecessary escalation and delays.

7.q: A project manager leads a technically strong team whose members have become passive and reluctant to take initiative on their work. To rebuild commitment, which TWO actions would BEST help the project manager increase ownership in this capable but disengaged team?
o: Focus solely on individual underperformance rather than team conditions
Increase approval layers so decisions feel controlled
Delegate appropriate authority while keeping outcomes clear
Remove all accountability until morale has improved
Involve the team in decisions that affect how work is delivered
7.w: Involvement and appropriate delegation increase ownership while still maintaining clarity over outcomes.

n.0: Focusing only on individuals may ignore leadership and team environment causes.
n.1: More approval layers usually reduce autonomy and engagement.
n.3: Removing accountability weakens ownership rather than building it.

7.q: A project is delivered on time and within budget, but the intended operational improvements are not realised and stakeholders are dissatisfied. Which judgement best reflects project success?
o: The project is partially successful because outputs were delivered
The project cannot be assessed without reviewing technical quality
The project is successful because it met time and cost constraints
The project is successful because governance objectives were met
The project is unsuccessful because benefits and stakeholder satisfaction were not achieved
7.w: Success is defined by benefits and stakeholder satisfaction, not just time, cost, and quality.

n.0: Outputs alone are insufficient to determine success.
n.1: The failure in benefits and satisfaction is already clear.
n.2: Time and cost alone do not define success.
n.3: Governance success does not equal project success.

7.q: On a systems upgrade project, requests to alter scope arrive regularly from different stakeholders, and the project manager has embedded the change process within the wider plan. What is a benefit of integrating change control into the project management plan?
o: Schedule and budget baselines stay fixed once changes are approved
Change requests are logged separately from the management plan
Only the project manager needs to authorise significant changes
Approved changes are applied before their impact has been assessed
All changes are documented and evaluated for impact on the entire project
7.w: Integrated change control maintains project alignment and records impacts.

n.0: Stakeholder approval is usually essential.
n.1: All changes, not just technical, must be managed.
n.2: Budgets and schedules may still change.
n.3: Ignoring changes can cause problems.

7.q: A project manager is justifying to a governance board why a Responsibility Assignment Matrix has been introduced on a complex delivery. Which TWO benefits result from using a Responsibility Assignment Matrix?
7.w: RAM clarifies roles and accountability.

7.q: Which TWO factors are critical when identifying stakeholders?
o: Their personal relationship with the project manager or team members
Their location within the organisational structure hierarchy only
Their potential influence on project outcomes and decisions
Their level of interest in the project and its objectives
Their preferred formatting style for project documentation outputs
7.w: Influence and interest are key factors in identifying and assessing stakeholders.

n.0: Personal relationships are not a key factor.
n.1: Location alone is insufficient.
n.4: Formatting preferences are not critical.

7.q: A stakeholder with high influence begins to oppose the project due to perceived lack of involvement. What should the project manager do first?
o: Escalate the issue to the project board
Engage directly to involve them in decisions
Send formal updates outlining decisions already made
7.w: High-influence stakeholders should be actively engaged and involved.

n.0: Escalation is premature.
n.2: Reducing communication worsens the issue.
n.3: One-way updates reduce engagement.
n.4: Detail does not address involvement.

7.q: A change has been proposed on a manufacturing project and the project manager is evaluating whether to put it forward for approval. Which of the following would justify a recommendation to approve the change?
o: The change is outside project scope
The change reduces overall project risk
The change increases project complexity unnecessarily
7.w: Risk reduction is a valid reason to approve a change.

n.0: Out-of-scope changes require rejection or redefinition.
n.2: Unnecessary complexity argues against approval.
n.3: Lack of benefits is a reason to reject.
n.4: Delays generally oppose approval.

7.q: A decision gate approves continuation despite marginal benefits because significant costs have already been incurred. What issue does this indicate?
7.w: Continuing due to sunk costs reflects escalation of commitment rather than rational decision-making.

n.0: Governance should challenge this bias.
n.2: This reflects poor decision-making, not effective risk management.
n.3: Forecasting is not the core issue here.
n.4: Alignment does not justify poor decisions.

7.q: An organisation is weighing a move to a fully projectised structure and wants to understand the governance effects before committing. It asks the PMO which results such a structure typically produces. Which TWO outcomes are most likely in a projectised organisation?
7.w: Projectised structures provide clear accountability and strong authority.

7.q: A new project involves multiple subcontractors and strict regulatory requirements. Why is it critical to implement robust governance arrangements in this context?
o: To accelerate the supplier procurement process
To monitor the marketing team's campaign performance
To reduce the number of governance meetings
To ensure policies and procedures are consistently followed
To remove the need for separate quality assurance
7.w: Governance ensures that project activities align with regulations and internal procedures, especially when subcontractors and compliance are involved.

n.0: While governance may influence procurement, its main role is broader.
n.1: Marketing performance is not the focus of governance structures.
n.2: Governance often increases structured communication, not reduces it.
n.4: Quality assurance is part of governance, not a result of avoiding it.

7.q: During requirements analysis, a stakeholder raises a need that cannot be justified when tested against the project's objectives. To keep the scope relevant and controlled, what should happen to this need?
o: The need should be excluded from project scope
It should be added to project baseline anyway
The team should allocate extra budget for it
It should become a high-priority risk
It should be escalated to project sponsors without review
7.w: Unjustified requirements should be excluded to keep the scope relevant and controlled.

n.1: Only justified needs should enter the baseline.
n.2: Budget should be allocated to agreed requirements.
n.3: Unjustified requirements are not automatically risks.
n.4: Escalation should follow analysis, not be automatic.

7.q: A project manager sets a milestone in the plan to mark the completion of a significant piece of work but does not define any acceptance criteria against which it will be judged complete. What is the most likely outcome of defining the milestone in this way?
o: More consistent reporting across the project stages
Reduced effort needed to validate the milestone output
Stronger stakeholder confidence in the milestone status
Faster agreement on when the milestone is complete
Ambiguity in determining whether the milestone is achieved
7.w: Without criteria, milestone completion becomes subjective and difficult to validate.

7.q: As a project reaches a defined business case review point, the governance board wants to focus its limited time on what genuinely matters. Which TWO activities are essential at business case review points?
o: Evaluating whether the project remains viable
7.w: Review points focus on viability reassessment.

7.q: A risk has been identified and assessed as high probability but low impact. What is the most appropriate next step?
o: Convert the risk into an issue
Define and implement an appropriate response strategy
7.w: All assessed risks require an appropriate response proportional to their impact and likelihood.

n.0: Assessment does not justify closure.
n.1: A risk is not yet an issue.
n.2: Ignoring risks increases exposure.
n.3: Escalation may not be necessary.

7.q: During a project review, the team discovers that certain tasks have taken longer than expected. Why is schedule optimisation valuable in this situation?
o: It removes the need for stakeholder reporting
It helps the team adjust plans to avoid further delays
It guarantees that no tasks will ever run late again
It allows quality standards to be ignored
7.w: Schedule optimisation allows the project to adapt and reduce the chance of further delays.

n.0: Reporting is still necessary.
n.2: Delays can be reduced, but not eliminated.
n.3: Quality must not be sacrificed.
n.4: Risks still need to be managed separately.

7.q: A sponsor wants assurance that variances from plan will be picked up promptly rather than surfacing too late to act on. Complete the statement: effective ______ of the business case ensures early detection of variances.
7.w: Monitoring the business case keeps track of performance against the baseline.

n.1: Delegation isn’t relevant to variance detection.
n.2: Closure happens at project end.
n.3: Documentation supports monitoring but isn’t the activity itself.
n.4: Planning is done upfront, not for variance detection.

7.q: On a software delivery project, a team holds a structured session in which each completed deliverable is formally examined against the agreed standards before sign-off. This activity is an example of which of the following?
7.w: Formal review against standards is a classic quality control activity.

n.0: Market analysis is for business, not quality.
n.1: Issues are managed elsewhere.
n.2: Resource levelling is unrelated.
n.3: Scope change manages deliverables, not reviews them.

7.q: The extended life cycle begins immediately after ______.
7.w: The extended life cycle starts after project closure, when the focus shifts to benefits and operations.

n.0: Initiation is the start of the project life cycle, not the extended cycle.
n.1: Design occurs within the delivery stage of the project.
n.2: Team formation is part of project startup activities.
n.3: Risk analysis is conducted during the project planning stage.

7.q: Whatever the pricing model, a project manager wants every proposed change to scope to be raised, assessed, approved and documented through a defined process rather than agreed informally. Which clause ensures scope changes are formally managed in any contract type?
7.w: Change control clauses mandate formal procedures for approving and documenting scope changes.

n.0: Audit covers record access, not scope management.
n.1: Termination covers contract end processes.
n.2: Overrun sharing is specific to target cost.
n.4: Escalation addresses price changes due to cost factors.

7.q: A project manager has just approved the scope and is preparing to build a detailed, bottom-up budget for the work to be delivered. Before any cost figures can be assembled with confidence, what is the first essential step the project manager should take?
o: Assign tasks randomly to available staff
Identify and list all project tasks and required resources
Increase the project’s contingency fund without analysis
Book meeting rooms for the project team
7.w: Identifying all tasks and resources is crucial to ensure all costs are captured in the budget.

n.0: Random task assignment is not best practice.
n.2: Contingency must be based on actual analysis.
n.3: Marketing slogans are unrelated to budgeting.
n.4: Meetings support planning but don’t drive budget creation.

7.q: A project adopts a fast, high-volume digital channel that pushes updates to stakeholders very quickly, but stakeholders report that important items are getting lost and overlooked among the many messages. What is the KEY disadvantage of this method?
7.w: Fast digital communication can lead to excessive information that stakeholders ignore.

n.1: Documentation may still exist.
n.2: Cost is not the main issue.
n.3: Reach is often broad.
n.4: Speed is high, not low.

7.q: In Herzberg’s Two-Factor Theory, “recognition” falls under which category?
7.w: Recognition is considered a motivator in Herzberg’s theory, driving job satisfaction.

n.0: Safety needs are part of Maslow’s model, not Herzberg’s.
n.1: Hygiene factors include salary and work conditions, not recognition.
n.2: Recognition is exclusively a motivator.
n.3: Recognition clearly affects satisfaction, so it cannot be neither.

7.q: A team leader deliberately rotates responsibilities so that each member is regularly stretched, challenged and kept engaged by varied, meaningful work. Which underlying assumption about people at work does this leadership behaviour best illustrate?
7.w: Task variety and challenge align with Theory Y’s assumption that work can be intrinsically motivating.

n.0: Herzberg’s motivators include recognition and achievement, but task rotation is Theory Y style.
n.2: Theory X is about control, not intrinsic motivation.
n.3: Safety needs are about stability, not variety.
n.4: Hygiene factors don’t drive engagement.

7.q: A software upgrade project has listed the following: 1) Updated software installed, 2) Faster system performance, 3) Reduced IT support costs. How should these be classified when defining project scope?
o: 1 is an outcome, 2 is a benefit, 3 is an output
1 is an output, 2 is an outcome, 3 is a benefit
1 is an outcome, 2 is an output, 3 is a benefit
1 is a benefit, 2 is an outcome, 3 is an output
1 is a benefit, 2 is an output, 3 is an outcome
7.w: Output: installed software; outcome: faster performance; benefit: reduced IT support costs.

n.0: Faster performance is an outcome, not a benefit or output.
n.2: The updated software is the output, not the outcome.
n.3: Reduced costs are a benefit, not an output.
n.4: The benefit is reduced IT support costs, not software installation.

7.q: In a software rollout, unrealistic stakeholder expectations led to frequent change requests. Which is NOT an expected result of managing those expectations?
7.w: Expectation management can guide agreement, but it cannot guarantee stakeholders will always agree on every detail.

n.0: Satisfaction generally improves when expectations align with deliverables.
n.1: Better planning of resources follows from clear expectations.
n.3: Fewer rework cycles occur when stakeholders know what to expect.
n.4: Priorities become clearer with transparent communication.

7.q: Which is NOT a valid negotiation approach?
7.w: "Zero-sum conflict" is not a recommended approach as it assumes one side wins only at the other's expense.

n.0: Win–win seeks mutual benefits.
n.2: Collaborative focuses on joint solutions.
n.3: Principled negotiation uses objective criteria.
n.4: Interest-based addresses underlying needs.

7.q: Midway through delivery, a manufacturing project falls behind schedule because its suppliers cannot provide key components on time, owing to worldwide material shortages beyond anyone's control. When reviewing the cause of the delay, which context factor is dominant?
7.w: Global shortages are external economic factors.

n.0: Expectations are not the cause.
n.1: Governance is not the cause.
n.2: Hierarchy is internal.
n.3: Scheduling is not the issue.

7.q: A project team joins forces with another organisation to deliver an innovation that neither party could have achieved on its own, allocating the opportunity to the partner best placed to realise it. Which risk response does this arrangement represent?
7.w: Sharing means allocating opportunity to a partner best able to realise it.

n.0: Acceptance means no active attempt to realise the opportunity.
n.1: Avoid is for threats, not opportunities.
n.2: Reject is not a formal positive risk response.
n.4: Reduction is for threats.

8.q: A project team knows a risk is unlikely but chooses to do nothing until it happens. What response is this?
8.w: Acceptance is choosing to tolerate a risk, taking no action until it materialises.

n.0: Share is for opportunities.
n.1: Transfer moves risk to another party.
n.2: Avoidance seeks to remove the risk proactively.
n.4: Exploit is for opportunities.

8.q: On a linear project, formal review points are placed between phases, and the work is only allowed to proceed once each has been passed. The project manager is explaining their purpose to the team. Which TWO roles do stage gates perform in a linear life cycle?
8.w: Stage gates enable decisions and approvals.

n.0: Risks remain.
n.1: Documentation remains important.
n.2: Governance still applies.

8.q: A project has experienced confusion over which documents are the latest versions. What is the BEST way to address this?
o: Reduce the number of project documents
Increase the frequency of project audits only
Let team members choose their own version
8.w: Status accounting keeps records of latest versions and approved changes.

n.0: Reducing documents doesn't solve version control.
n.1: Audits alone do not prevent version issues.
n.2: Allowing personal choice undermines control.
n.3: Verbal communication can increase confusion.

8.q: A project manager discovers an unplanned scope increase midway through execution. What should they do first regarding the business case?
o: Reassign project resources to cover the extra work
Inform the sponsor immediately without any impact analysis
Revise the requirements document to add the scope
Review the business case against the original baseline
Update the project schedule to absorb the change
8.w: The first step is to compare the change against the original business case baseline to assess impact.

n.0: Reassigning resources is premature before impact analysis.
n.1: Informing without analysis skips the necessary assessment.
n.2: Revising requirements should follow a business case review.
n.4: Updating the schedule comes after assessing impact on the business case.

8.q: A project sponsor wants a single visual that shows, over time, how actual benefits compare against what was originally forecast. In benefits management, which tool would you use to visualise actual versus planned benefits over time?
8.w: A benefits dashboard displays real vs planned benefits trends.

n.0: Issue log records problems.
n.1: Quality register tracks quality metrics.
n.2: Scope baseline defines scope status.
n.4: Communication matrix maps communication paths.

8.q: On a project, two stakeholders come into conflict because they hold differing expectations about what the project should deliver. What should the project manager do first to address the situation?
o: Delay resolution until the next reporting cycle
Support the stakeholder with more influence
Ignore the conflict if progress is unaffected
8.w: Early facilitation helps align expectations and reduce conflict.

n.0: Escalation is not the first step.
n.1: Delays worsen the issue.
n.3: Biasing one stakeholder increases conflict.
n.4: Ignoring conflict risks escalation.

8.q: A project manager is building an effective communication management plan and wants to draw the most useful information from the completed stakeholder analysis. Which of the following are critical inputs to that plan?
8.w: Preferences and influence determine how and with whom communications are tailored.

n.1: Quality metrics relate to deliverables, not stakeholder communications.
n.2: The charter and scope are project initiation outputs.
n.3: Procurement methods are procurement inputs, not communication.
n.4: Risk appetite and budget are separate domains.

8.q: A software development project receives multiple change requests each week. What is a key advantage of iterative life cycles when managing change control?
o: They use only annual change control reviews
They accommodate frequent changes without disrupting the project flow
They ignore change requests to maintain stability
They eliminate the need for change logs
They delay all changes until the end of the project
8.w: Iterative life cycles are flexible and can accommodate ongoing change without major disruption.

n.0: Frequent reviews occur in iterative, not just annual.
n.2: Ignoring change requests is not best practice.
n.3: Change logs are still required for accountability.
n.4: Delaying all changes is not how iterative projects operate.

8.q: Which is NOT an objective of negotiation in procurement?
o: Defeat the supplier on every point
8.w: Negotiation aims for an agreement that meets objectives and protects the relationship; winning every point at the other party's expense damages trust and long-term value.

n.0: Terms and conditions form the negotiated agreement.
n.1: Controlling whole-life cost is a common objective.
n.2: Creating mutual value is the aim of principled negotiation.
n.3: Deliverables must be clearly defined.

8.q: On a project that has been reorganised, the RACI matrix still reflects the old team layout and no longer matches how the project is actually staffed. What can happen as a result of this mismatch?
o: The immediate closure of the whole project
A reduced need for communication between members
Faster and easier decision making across the team
The automatic identification of every project risk
Confusion and missed responsibilities due to misaligned assignments
8.w: A RACI that does not match the real team structure leads to confusion and possible errors.

n.0: Projects will continue until closed properly.
n.1: Communication is even more important if RACI is unclear.
n.2: Decisions may actually be delayed if roles are unclear.
n.3: Risks must still be actively identified and managed.

8.q: At a review point, a project is forecast to exceed cost tolerances but still deliver strong benefits. What should the business case support?
o: A reassessment of viability before deciding to continue
Automatic continuation because the benefits remain strong
Immediate termination because cost tolerances will be breached
Adjusting cost tolerances to absorb the overspend
Delegation of the decision to the delivery team
8.w: Review points require reassessment of all components before continuation decisions.

8.q: Which TWO risks arise from poor progress reporting?
o: Misalignment between stakeholders and project team
8.w: Poor reporting leads to delays in decisions and misalignment.

8.q: A sponsor wants the delivery approach to give the strongest possible control through predefined documentation, formal reviews and stage approvals on a safety-critical project. Which life cycle best offers this level of control?
8.w: Linear life cycles provide control via documentation, structured reviews, and defined stage boundaries.

n.0: Iterative models focus on adaptability, not rigid control.
n.1: Hybrid offers some control but less than pure linear models.
n.2: Prototyping emphasises speed and user feedback over structure.
n.4: Agile values lightweight documentation and flexibility.

8.q: During delivery, a key deliverable fails a quality control test against its agreed specification, and the project manager must decide how the team responds before the output can be accepted. What should the project team do next?
o: Escalate the failure immediately for additional funding approval
Relax the success criteria so the deliverable passes
Record the result and release the deliverable regardless
Investigate and correct the issue to meet success criteria
Reassign the deliverable to a different team member
8.w: Non-conformity must be corrected so outputs meet success criteria.

n.0: Budget changes may not solve the quality issue.
n.1: Approval must wait until criteria are met.
n.2: Ignoring quality problems leads to poor outcomes.
n.4: Management changes are not the first action.

8.q: A project manager wants to understand when it is appropriate to revisit and improve the schedule during delivery rather than leaving it untouched. What should trigger schedule optimisation during the project life cycle?
o: Any minor variation that stays within agreed tolerances
Sign-off of the project's initial requirements document
Formal closure of the project after final handover
Routine completion of each weekly status report
Discovery of delays, new risks, or opportunities to improve efficiency
8.w: Optimisation is prompted by significant events like delays, risks, or new efficiencies.

n.0: Lessons learned come after project closure.
n.1: The charter comes before detailed planning.
n.2: Not every minor issue justifies major schedule changes.
n.3: Budget approval is a milestone but not the sole trigger.

8.q: A group of stakeholders is nervous about the level of uncertainty surrounding a complex project. How does effective risk management benefit stakeholder confidence?
o: It removes the need for communication
It shortens the approval process automatically
It demonstrates proactive control over uncertainty
8.w: Managing risks shows stakeholders that uncertainty is recognised and addressed.

n.0: Communication remains important.
n.1: Cost overruns may still occur.
n.2: Changes must still be controlled.
n.3: Approval processes do not change automatically.

8.q: A project manager under schedule pressure begins driving the team mainly through deadlines, criticism and fear of consequences. Considering the effect of this style, which TWO risks are MOST associated with relying mainly on pressure and fear to drive project performance?
o: Quality normally improves because people feel safer challenging issues
Short-term compliance may replace genuine commitment
Learning and improvement may reduce because people avoid exposing problems
Trust is likely to increase because expectations are strict
Team members may become more willing to report mistakes early
8.w: Fear-based leadership can produce compliance but reduces openness, learning, commitment and long-term performance.

n.0: People are less likely to challenge quality issues when they fear blame.
n.3: Strictness without safety often reduces trust.
n.4: Fear usually reduces early reporting of mistakes.

8.q: A project manager is deciding how best to convey different pieces of project information to a varied set of recipients and wants to select the medium sensibly each time. Which TWO factors should MOST influence the choice of communication method?
o: Channel used on the previous project
8.w: The method should suit the message and the recipients. Urgency decides how fast and direct the channel must be, and the audience's needs (interest, influence, preferences, level of understanding) decide the format, detail and channel.

n.0: Communication is tailored to the receiver, not to the sender's convenience.
n.3: Good communication invites feedback; choosing a method to avoid it undermines engagement and understanding.
n.4: Reusing the last project's channel is habit; it does not respond to these recipients or this message.

8.q: On a delivery-phase IT project, the project manager grows uneasy about how closely the sponsor is engaging with the technical team. Which TWO situations indicate inappropriate sponsor involvement in operational delivery?
o: The sponsor challenges whether the business case remains valid
The sponsor gives daily instructions to technical team members
The sponsor reviews whether benefits remain achievable
The sponsor directly reallocates team tasks without the project manager
The sponsor approves a major funding decision
8.w: Directly reallocating tasks and instructing team members are operational delivery activities that should sit with the project manager.

8.q: A project team includes individuals with a range of working styles, needs and communication preferences. The project manager wants to make sure each person is able to participate on an equal footing. Which of the following is a fair way to support an individual's contribution in a team?
o: Only recognising contributions from senior staff
Adapting communication methods to meet their needs
Expecting everyone to conform to a single style
8.w: Adapting to individual needs facilitates fair participation.

n.0: Recognition should be inclusive of all.
n.2: A single style may exclude some team members.
n.3: Different preferences should be respected.
n.4: Feedback opportunities should be open to everyone.

8.q: A project team is drawing up the sustainability objectives that will guide decisions throughout a construction programme. Reviewing a draft list of priorities put forward by different members, which of the following is NOT a genuine sustainability priority in project management?
8.w: Maximising environmental degradation conflicts directly with sustainability goals.

n.0: Efficient energy use is central to environmental sustainability.
n.2: Supporting communities aligns with the social dimension of sustainability.
n.3: Long-term viability is a core objective of sustainable practice.
n.4: Reducing waste is a key sustainability priority.

8.q: Pricing bids exceed the project's budget. The team seeks the range where both parties can agree. Which concept guides this effort?
8.w: ZOPA defines the range in which buyer and supplier expectations overlap.

n.0: POs are purchase orders issued after agreements.
n.1: WBS is a work breakdown structure, not negotiation-related.
n.2: RFQs request pricing but don't define agreement zones.
n.3: SLAs set post-award performance commitments.

8.q: A project manager is explaining to the team what practical steps resource levelling involves when demand exceeds capacity. Which TWO actions are part of the resource levelling process?
8.w: Levelling involves adjusting schedules and resource allocation.

n.1: Dependencies must be respected.
n.2: Deadlines may change.
n.4: Scope is unrelated.

8.q: A project manager observes that, several weeks in, the team is still struggling to reach the performing stage of its development and remains stuck in earlier stages. Which of the following is most likely to be causing this delay in the team reaching peak performance?
o: Unresolved conflicts and lack of trust
8.w: Conflicts and mistrust can keep a team stuck in the earlier stages.

n.0: Good communication helps teams progress.
n.1: Complementary skills benefit teamwork.
n.2: Clear goals speed up development.
n.3: Organisational support usually helps teams develop.

8.q: A Cost Breakdown Structure (CBS) shows costs exceeding budget, but the Work Breakdown Structure appears accurate. What is the most likely issue?
o: The product breakdown structure was left partially incomplete
Key dependencies between activities are missing from the network
The stakeholders have not been properly engaged throughout
The project schedule contains errors in its activity durations
Costs are not properly aligned to work packages
8.w: CBS must align with WBS; misalignment leads to inaccurate cost tracking.

8.q: Keen to keep the project moving, a project manager takes several strategic decisions that affect the business case without first consulting the sponsor. At the next review the sponsor is unaware these decisions were made. What risk does this create?
8.w: Strategic decisions should align with sponsor oversight.

8.q: An engineering firm is concerned that placing staff into permanent, dedicated delivery teams could reduce how easily people draw on specialists based in other departments. Which of the following structures most likely limits access to shared functional expertise?
8.w: Project-based teams may not have regular access to specialists from other departments.

n.0: Hybrid models often maintain access to functional support.
n.1: Balanced matrix promotes collaboration between functions.
n.3: Functional structures centralise expertise.
n.4: Matrix structures allow sharing of specialists.

8.q: A project team is delivering work in another country and must comply with the standards that apply in that jurisdiction. To be confident they are following the correct requirements, where can they find information on these local standards?
o: Assumptions based on similar past projects
Informal advice from local project team members
Standards already applied in the home country
General guidance issued by professional networks
8.w: Local authorities publish the standards that apply in their jurisdiction.

n.0: Fiction books are not a reliable source.
n.1: Preferences do not override standards.
n.3: Travel guides are not about professional standards.
n.4: Interpretation must be guided by official sources.

8.q: A project manager wants a single set of actions that will both reduce dissatisfaction and actively motivate the team, addressing hygiene factors and motivators together as Herzberg describes. Which of the following approaches would most likely satisfy both needs simultaneously?
o: Raising salaries WITHOUT enriching the job content
Improving workplace facilities AND offering credit for high performance
Improving job security AND increasing supervision levels
Delegating more responsibility AND creating clearer routes to advancement
Enforcing stricter policies AND closely monitoring attendance
8.w: Working conditions are a Herzberg hygiene factor (reduces dissatisfaction) and recognition for achievement is a motivator (creates satisfaction), so this pair addresses both.

n.0: Pay is a hygiene factor; without enriching the work there is no motivator.
n.2: Job security and supervision are both hygiene factors; neither actively motivates.
n.3: Responsibility and advancement are both motivators; no hygiene factor is addressed, so dissatisfaction may remain.
n.4: Policies and supervision are hygiene factors, and tightening them is more likely to increase dissatisfaction.

8.q: Which statement about prioritising requirements is TRUE?
o: It guarantees all requirements are delivered at once
It only applies to IT projects
It helps ensure that resources focus on the most valuable outcomes
It prevents the need for stakeholder engagement
It is the sole responsibility of the project sponsor
8.w: Prioritisation ensures focus on the requirements with greatest value.

n.0: Not all requirements are delivered together.
n.1: Prioritisation is important for all project types.
n.3: Stakeholder engagement is still required.
n.4: It requires input from multiple roles.

8.q: Some months after a project has handed over its outputs, the sponsor commissions a benefits review to judge whether the anticipated value has materialised. Conducted after project completion, this benefits review primarily helps the organisation to do what?
o: confirm that the outputs met their acceptance criteria
compare realised benefits with original forecasts
8.w: A post-project benefits review compares the benefits actually realised with those forecast in the business case.

n.0: Output acceptance is confirmed at handover, not in a benefits review.
n.2: Releasing contingency is part of financial close-down.
n.3: Individual performance is not the focus of a benefits review.
n.4: The project has closed; there is no schedule to re-baseline.

8.q: A public-sector organisation delivering a new customer service system adopts an extended life cycle that continues beyond handover into operational use. A stakeholder questions why this additional phase has been built into the approach. Why is a post-project phase included in an extended life cycle?
o: To monitor whether intended benefits are realised
To ensure outputs are documented correctly
8.w: The post-project phase focuses on benefits realisation.

n.1: It serves a purpose, not delay.
n.2: Resource reassignment is not the purpose.
n.3: Documentation is not the primary aim.
n.4: Governance remains relevant.

8.q: A projectised organisation is able to deliver individual projects quickly, but senior management notices that approaches, reporting and quality vary widely from one project to the next. Which governance adjustment would best address this inconsistency?
o: Standardise processes through central governance frameworks
8.w: Central governance frameworks improve consistency without eliminating project autonomy.

8.q: A reviewer is examining how a project team has applied the power/interest grid and finds that engagement is not matching stakeholder needs. Which TWO of the following indicate the grid is being used ineffectively?
o: Failure to update stakeholder positions as their influence or interest changes
Regular review and adjustment of stakeholder engagement strategies over time
Misclassification of stakeholder influence levels leading to poor prioritisation
Clear segmentation of stakeholders based on their power and interest levels
Consistent alignment of engagement approaches with stakeholder categories
8.w: Misclassification and lack of updates indicate ineffective use.

n.1: Reviewing strategies is good practice.
n.3: Segmentation is correct practice.
n.4: Alignment indicates effective use.

8.q: A project manager is determined that the solution developed will be as close to optimal as possible for the organisation. Which combination of actions should they prioritise?
o: Rely solely on the original requirements list throughout
Evaluate requirements for value, prioritise delivery, and incorporate feedback iteratively
Let the team self-organise without any stakeholder input
Complete all technical tasks first and weigh value later
Deliver every requested feature regardless of its value
8.w: An optimal solution is built by evaluating, prioritising and adapting based on feedback.

n.0: Requirements can change as more is learned.
n.2: Leadership and input improve outcomes.
n.3: Value should inform all technical decisions.
n.4: Value analysis prevents waste.

8.q: On a project where the cost estimates keep being revised, each change ripples out and disrupts other elements of the plan, provoking disagreement among the team. Conflict arising from which of the following does this best describe?
8.w: Budget volatility—shifting cost estimates—can trigger conflicts elsewhere.

n.0: Process automation reduces manual errors, not conflict.
n.2: Clear governance mitigates rather than causes conflict.
n.3: Stable requirements are not a source of conflict.
n.4: Team alignment prevents conflicts.

8.q: A post-project review focuses only on what went wrong, leading to reduced morale and resistance to future reviews. What is the MOST appropriate improvement?
o: Focus only on financial performance to simplify the evaluation
Replace formal reviews with occasional informal feedback sessions
Restrict the review to senior stakeholders and managers only
Balance evaluation by capturing both successes and areas for improvement
Avoid discussing any problems in order to protect morale
8.w: Effective reviews capture both positive and negative insights to support learning without damaging morale.

n.0: Financial focus ignores broader lessons.
n.1: Informal feedback lacks structure for learning.
n.2: Excluding team input reduces insight.
n.4: Avoiding issues prevents learning.

8.q: Partway through the project, a newly formed team has begun openly disagreeing over roles and priorities, with tension rising between individuals as they compete for influence. At this stage of team development, which leadership response is MOST appropriate?
o: Apply strict control to suppress disagreement and enforce compliance
Provide facilitation to manage conflict and clarify roles and expectations
Delegate all decisions to the team to encourage independence
Escalate interpersonal issues immediately to senior stakeholders
Avoid intervening to allow conflicts to resolve without influence
8.w: During storming, leaders should facilitate resolution of conflict and provide clarity to guide the team forward.

n.0: Suppressing disagreement can damage trust and cohesion.
n.2: Full delegation may worsen unresolved conflict.
n.3: Escalation avoids addressing team dynamics directly.
n.4: Non-intervention can allow conflict to escalate.

8.q: During a scenario where a project has missed several milestones, which benefit of a decision gate review would be most valuable?
o: Eliminating the need to report to sponsors
Enabling a go/no-go decision to realign resources
8.w: In such a scenario, the gate allows stakeholders to decide whether to continue, pause, or stop to reallocate resources.

n.0: Reporting remains essential even after a gate.
n.1: Gate reviews do not reduce meeting frequency.
n.3: Success cannot be guaranteed by a gate.
n.4: Risk management cannot be fully outsourced.

8.q: A project manager is drafting the success criteria for a new initiative and wants to ensure the measures capture more than simply delivering the work on time. Which TWO factors should be included when defining project success criteria?
8.w: Benefits and stakeholder satisfaction are key success measures.

n.0: Governance avoidance is not relevant.
n.3: Time alone is insufficient.
n.4: Workload is not a success criterion.

9.q: A newly formed delivery team needs someone to translate project objectives into clear task allocations and make sure everyone knows what they are expected to produce. Which of the following roles is primarily responsible for ensuring the project team understands their assigned work?
9.w: The project manager communicates objectives and manages task allocation.

n.1: The product owner manages product priorities, not task allocation.
n.2: The sponsor offers high-level guidance, not task instructions.
n.3: The change manager handles change impacts, not daily task clarity.
n.4: Senior users give input but don't lead the team.

9.q: A project manager wants to introduce something that will genuinely raise team members' job satisfaction rather than merely stop them becoming dissatisfied. Within Herzberg's theory, which of the following is a motivator that directly enhances job satisfaction?
9.w: Recognition is a motivator that fosters satisfaction; the others are hygiene factors.

n.1: Salary is a hygiene factor.
n.2: Supervision quality is treated as hygiene in Herzberg’s model.
n.3: Working conditions are hygiene factors.
n.4: Policy is a hygiene factor.

9.q: Ready to go to market, a project manager needs the formal document that invites suppliers to submit their bids for the work. The document that formally invites vendors to submit bids is an ______.
9.w: An Invitation to Tender (ITT) is the formal request for bidders to submit offers.

n.1: The SOW defines deliverables, not the invitation format.
n.2: Notice to Proceed is issued post-award.
n.3: Change Orders modify existing contracts.
n.4: Requisitions are internal purchase requests.

9.q: A project manager is setting up the CBS for a major IT upgrade. What information should be included in each CBS category?
o: Purchase order numbers and supplier contact details for each
Subjective opinions on whether each listed cost is justified
The names of external stakeholders linked to each cost
Estimated costs, responsible person, and timeline for each element
Colour codes and formatting preferences for each cost element
9.w: Each CBS element should list its cost, who manages it, and the timing.

n.0: Birthdays are not relevant.
n.1: Objective data is required for budget control.
n.2: Stakeholder names belong in other plans.
n.4: Colour codes may help visually, but aren’t required.

9.q: During response planning, a project manager looks for ways to make a favourable event both more likely to occur and more beneficial if it does. Which response strategy is concerned with increasing the likelihood or impact of a positive risk in this way?
9.w: Enhancement aims to make opportunities more likely or impactful.

n.0: Reject is not a formal response to enhance opportunities.
n.1: Transfer is about passing risk to another party.
n.3: Avoid is for threats.
n.4: Reduction is for negative risks.

9.q: During an audit review of a regulated project, the assurance team discovers that a critical compliance standard was missed during the previous phase. In this scenario, what does the audit review process enable the project to do?
o: Rapid identification and correction of the non-compliant area
Immediate cancellation of the project without review
Automatic distribution of performance rewards to staff
Disregarding the concerns raised by stakeholders
Halting all further compliance monitoring efforts
9.w: Audits enable rapid detection and correction of compliance failures.

n.1: Cancellation without review is not a standard process.
n.2: Rewards are unrelated to audit findings.
n.3: Stakeholder concerns remain important.
n.4: Compliance efforts must continue.

9.q: A sponsor asks a project manager to explain, in a single statement, why so much effort is spent coordinating the project's schedule with the organisation's ongoing operations. Which statement best summarises the need to manage dependencies between project and business-as-usual activities?
o: Project schedules should never influence live BAU operations
Managed dependencies remove the need for a project schedule
BAU activities take priority over project work at all times
Unmanaged dependencies can lead to project delays and operational disruption
Dependencies always shorten the overall project delivery time
9.w: If dependencies are ignored, both project and business operations can suffer, causing delays and disruption.

n.0: Good management can actually control or reduce costs.
n.1: Benefits are not guaranteed just by managing dependencies.
n.2: Project schedules should be tailored, not identical to BAU.
n.4: Some risks are always present, even if dependencies are managed.

9.q: After issuing a tender, a project manager receives bids that differ widely in price and approach and needs a consistent, objective basis for comparing them. Which should the procurement strategy guide?
9.w: An evaluation methodology with weighted criteria gives a consistent, objective basis for comparing bids that differ in price and approach.

n.0: Change control manages changes after the baseline is set.
n.2: Make-or-buy decides whether to procure at all, before tenders are issued.
n.3: Close-out happens at the end of the contract, not when comparing bids.
n.4: Debriefing follows the award decision; it does not compare bids.

9.q: A project manager is planning when to keep stakeholders informed about changes moving through the control process, from request through evaluation to a final decision. At what stage in the change control process is stakeholder communication most critical?
o: Only if the change is rejected
Throughout the entire change control process
9.w: Effective communication throughout ensures transparency and alignment.

n.0: Project closure is not the only time for communication.
n.1: Stakeholders should be informed regardless of approval.
n.2: Communication after implementation only is insufficient.
n.3: Communication is needed beyond submission.

9.q: A portfolio contains several very different initiatives, and the PMO wants to identify which of them would gain most from a hybrid life cycle. Which of the following projects would most likely benefit from a hybrid approach?
o: A public opinion survey requiring no iteration or feature change
A short marketing brochure with a single fixed delivery deadline
An IT system with strict security protocols and agile feature delivery
A civil engineering build with no anticipated design change throughout
A one-day internal training workshop with a settled agenda
9.w: Hybrid life cycles allow regulated environments (security) to benefit from agile feature delivery.

n.0: No iteration = no need for hybrid; linear fits better.
n.1: Fixed-scope marketing projects suit linear life cycles.
n.3: Civil projects are typically linear due to their structure.
n.4: Training workshops are usually simple and linear.

9.q: While finalising a transition plan, a project manager needs to agree who will take ownership of the risks being transferred to the receiving organisation as the new service goes live. She wants the right people around the table to reach that agreement. Which two stakeholders should be involved to agree risk transfer in a transition plan?
9.w: Operations managers and risk owners jointly agree on who will assume specific transition risks.

n.1: Facilities staff support logistics but don’t own transition risks.
n.2: Marketing and design roles are unrelated to risk ownership in transition.
n.3: Competitors are not internal decision-makers for risk transfer.
n.4: Shareholders/customers are recipients of value but not day-to-day risk owners.

9.q: The purpose of an audit review is to ________.
o: verify adherence to defined procedures and standards
9.w: Audit reviews verify that procedures and standards are being followed correctly.

n.0: Marketing planning is not an audit task.
n.1: Firewall configuration is IT’s domain.
n.2: Hiring is HR’s responsibility.
n.3: Promotional design is marketing work.

9.q: A project manager identifies that several activities appear independent but later discovers delays due to hidden dependencies. What is the most likely cause?
o: The timeline was too aggressive for the project scope
The critical path was incorrectly calculated
Activities were incorrectly sequenced due to incomplete dependency identification
Resources were not allocated efficiently across tasks
9.w: Hidden dependencies typically arise from incomplete identification during planning, leading to sequencing issues and delays.

9.q: During a workshop, a project team is populating the standard four quadrants of a SWOT analysis for their programme. As they check that every heading is a genuine SWOT category, which of the following is NOT one of the four recognised categories?
9.w: Solutions is not one of SWOT’s four categories.

n.0: Weaknesses is a valid SWOT category.
n.2: Threats is a valid SWOT category.
n.3: Opportunities is a valid SWOT category.
n.4: Strengths is a valid SWOT category.

9.q: A communication plan helps to ______ misunderstandings among stakeholders.
9.w: By defining channels, frequency, and content, a plan reduces ambiguity and misunderstandings.

n.0: Maximising misunderstandings is counter to the purpose of a communication plan.
n.1: Ignoring misunderstandings would worsen stakeholder relations.
n.2: Complicating matters is not a benefit of planning communications.
n.3: Encouraging misunderstandings defeats clear communication objectives.

9.q: A projectised organisation running many concurrent projects finds that specialist staff and equipment are frequently duplicated and under-used across teams. Senior management asks the PMO to identify the underlying structural cause. What is the underlying structural issue?
9.w: Projectised structures can lack resource efficiency due to duplication across projects.

9.q: Which TWO factors represent trade-offs when choosing written communication?
9.w: Written methods improve record and clarity but reduce interaction and flexibility.

n.0: Accuracy and detail are not opposing factors here.
n.2: Cost and quality are not the main trade-offs.
n.3: Written communication does not inherently reduce reach.

9.q: A project manager needs to ensure that every change to project scope is fully traceable. Which process best achieves this?
9.w: Configuration control tracks and authorises all changes, ensuring traceability.

n.0: Market research is unrelated to configuration management.
n.1: Stakeholder analysis relates to people, not changes.
n.2: Issue management focuses on problems, not traceability.
n.3: Schedule management is about time, not configuration items.

9.q: At the end of a phase, a project manager prepares the deliverables for scrutiny by the project board at a decision gate before the next phase is authorised. In governance terms, the decision gate review helps to do what before approving the next phase?
o: confirm that deliverables meet acceptance criteria
9.w: Gates confirm that deliverables satisfy defined acceptance criteria before progression.

n.0: Card printing is administrative.
n.1: Donor funding closure is not part of gate reviews.
n.2: Brochure publication is unrelated.
n.4: Consultant hiring is not the gate’s main purpose.

9.q: Following closure, a post-project review identifies missed benefits due to lack of operational readiness. What should have been addressed earlier?
9.w: Operational readiness and transition planning are critical to benefit realisation.

n.0: Resource levelling affects efficiency, not adoption.
n.1: Reporting does not ensure operational readiness.
n.2: Configuration baseline does not ensure adoption.
n.3: Procurement is unrelated to readiness.

9.q: A project manager wants to use recognition and reward to lift the performance of the delivery team over the course of the project. Which approach is MOST likely to be effective?
o: Use recognition mainly to compensate for unclear objectives
Recognise only senior team members because their work has greater project impact
Recognise visible effort only at the end of the project to avoid distraction
Link recognition to specific behaviours and outcomes that support project objectives
Give identical praise to all team members regardless of contribution
9.w: Recognition is most useful when it is specific, timely and connected to behaviours that improve project performance.

n.0: Recognition cannot compensate for lack of clear objectives.
n.1: Recognition should reflect contribution, not seniority alone.
n.2: Delayed recognition loses impact and may not reinforce desired behaviours.
n.4: Generic praise can feel meaningless and may not influence performance.

9.q: A project manager is assessing whether particular team members will genuinely be available to deliver the planned work. When assessing resource availability during planning, which TWO factors should be considered?
o: Format of the project highlight report
Earned value of completed work packages
9.w: Availability depends on what people are already committed to (other projects, BAU work, leave) and on whether the people who are free have the skills and competence the work needs. Both are checked against the resource requirements from the WBS and estimates.

n.0: The report format is a communication choice and has no bearing on resource availability.
n.1: Power and interest come from stakeholder analysis and shape engagement, not whether team members are free to do the work.
n.4: Earned value measures performance on work already done; it says nothing about whether people are available for planned work.

9.q: To preserve an important working relationship, a team member decides to set aside their own preference on a minor design point and go along with what a colleague wants instead. Which Thomas-Kilmann conflict mode involves prioritising the other party's concerns over your own?
9.w: Accommodating emphasizes others’ concerns above one’s own.

n.0: Competing prioritises one’s own concerns over others.
n.1: Avoiding withdraws from the conflict.
n.2: Collaborating seeks win-win solutions.
n.4: Compromising finds a middle ground.

9.q: A project delivers all outputs successfully, but no mechanism exists to track whether expected benefits are realised. What is the primary failure?
o: Benefits management has not been defined or implemented
The governance structure is too complex
The project manager has not controlled delivery effectively
9.w: Benefits must be tracked and managed beyond delivery; otherwise value cannot be confirmed.

9.q: At the start of an organisational change programme, a project manager is planning how to bring a diverse group of stakeholders to a shared view of what the project will achieve. When seeking to align stakeholder expectations, which TWO factors are critical?
o: Limiting involvement to the most senior stakeholders
Detailed earned value reporting to every stakeholder
Clear communication of scope and objectives
9.w: Expectations are aligned by being clear and honest about what the project will and will not deliver (scope and objectives), and by understanding what each stakeholder needs and why, so gaps can be surfaced and resolved early.

n.0: Leaving out less senior stakeholders leaves their expectations unmanaged, which causes dissatisfaction later even if targets are met.
n.1: Earned value data is performance information for those controlling the project; it does not create a shared view of what will be delivered.
n.2: One format for everyone ignores the need to tailor communication to each stakeholder, so it can hinder alignment.

9.q: Once a change request has been fully evaluated, the process calls for a recommendation to be prepared before the change authority decides. What is the primary reason for conducting a recommendation step after evaluating a change request?
o: To carry out the detailed impact analysis of the change
